usage.callShape: GET https://netintel-production-440c.up.railway.app/cron-parser/explain?expression=<cron>&timezone=UTC&count=5 — params go in the query string (GET, no body)
usage.outputShape: body.explanation (plain English), body.is_valid (bool), body.fields{minute,hour,day_of_month,month,day_of_week}, body.next_runs[] (ISO timestamps), body.score, body.grade, body.warnings[], body.findings[]
quirks: This is a GET endpoint — pass expression/timezone/count as URL query-string params, NOT a JSON body (despite inputSchema being object-shaped).
expression is required and must be URL-encoded (spaces -> %20, asterisks -> %2A).
count defaults to 5, max 20; timezone defaults to UTC (IANA strings).
usage.guide: Call GET https://netintel-production-440c.up.railway.app/cron-parser/explain with the cron expression in the query string, e.g. ?expression=0%209%20%2A%20%2A%201&timezone=UTC&count=5. Pay $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Read the plain-English meaning from body.explanation, validity from body.is_valid, and upcoming fire times from body.next_runs[]. The expression value must be URL-encoded.
